parts.premise:
Students in high-achieving communities who spend too much time on homework experience more stress, physical health problems, a lack of balance, and even alienation from society, Stanford senior lecturer Denise Pope found.

Denise Pope portrait; she is standing in hallway of CERAS building

A Stanford researcher found that too much homework can negatively affect kids, especially their lives away from school, where family, friends and activities matter.
parts.hypothesis: A study shows that early elementary students receive too much homework.
